fact: UNDP and ICTAM, with the ICT Minister present, launched the Digital Literacy Advocates programme: 30 certified university students are each to train 100 community members, 3,000 Malawians in all.
The University of Malawi and UNDP launched Nzeru Hub, a free digital learning platform for students and underserved communities offering digital skills courses, per UNIMA and UNDP.
The Secretary for Information and Digitalization says 10 tech hubs under the World Bank-funded Digital Malawi Project have taught digital skills to over 19,000 youths, women and elderly people.
Ministry of Information and Digitalisation said it has equipped 19,000 youths with digital literacy skills.
The Public Private Partnership Commission listed digital skills training for 10,000 Malawians among initiatives under the World Bank-funded Digital Malawi Acceleration Project.
The DIGMAP project, run by the Ministry with the PPPC and World Bank funding, equipped over 19,000 youths, women and the elderly with digital skills; locations are not stated.
A study by Malawi's National Statistical Office with MACRA found only 1.4% of Malawians possess digital skills.
